chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hassan (peace be upon him) about fasting in the month, how is it? He said: Three days in the month, one day in every ten days. Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, says: 'Whoever comes with a good deed, he shall have ten like it.' Three days in the month is fasting for the whole time.

key_terms.عَشْر: Ten (referring to the ten-day periods of the month)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for fasting three days a month in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the virtue of the 'Ayyam al-Beed' (white days) fasting, linking the monthly practice to the concept of 'fasting of the year' through the Quranic multiplier of ten deeds. In Shia jurisprudence, this is often understood as equivalent to fasting 30 days (10x3), though some scholars interpret it as equivalent to the entire year's reward due to the cumulative merit of consistency. The narration underscores the spiritual economy of good deeds, encouraging regularity in worship beyond obligatory fasts.
